newsitem.title: USA: Trigen gets committment for 3 projects.
newsitem.headline: Trigen gets committment for 3 projects.

text.p: Trigen Energy said on Monday it has received letters of intent for three new U.S. projects that could generate $20 million in annual revenues when completed and $425 million in revenues over the life of the contracts.

The Trigen-Cinergy Solutions partnership has signed letters of intent to acquire, upgrade and operate energy assets at two food-processing facilities in the Mid-West that are expected to generate annual revenues of $9 million, Trigen said in a statement.
Trigen said the work will include the installation of two of Trigen's factory-built standardized cogeneration units to provide electricity and steam.

Trigen has also signed a letter of intent to install standardized cogeneration units and back pressure steam turbines at a manufacturing plant on Long Island in a project expected to produce annual revenues of $5 million, the company said.
Trigen said its second quarter results reflected higher production costs for the start up of the new Prince Edward Island facility, but its costs are expected to decline in the next few months.
In addition, Trigen and its partner, Peoples Energy, closed their Illinois development office to cut costs, which led to a second quarter charge.

The company's 170 megawatt Grays Ferry Cogeneration Project is expected to be commissioned in the fourth quarter, which is expected to add $0.10 to $0.15 a share each quarter during the early years of operation, Trigen said.
